MISC_PA_01.name: Perimeter-Area Conflation
MISC_PA_01.description: Student calculates area (length × breadth) when perimeter (2 × (l + b)) is requested, or vice versa.
MISC_PA_01.evidence_trigger: Student chooses 6 × 3 = 18 when asked for area of a 6x3 rectangle, or confuses unit dimensions (cm vs sq cm).
MISC_PA_01.scaffolding_guidance: Anchor with boundary walk analogy: perimeter is the fence length; area is the grass inside.

MISC_PA_02.name: Partial Boundary Summation
MISC_PA_02.description: Student adds only length and breadth (l + b) instead of all four sides 2 × (l + b).
MISC_PA_02.evidence_trigger: Selecting 9 cm for a 6x3 rectangle instead of 18 cm.
MISC_PA_02.scaffolding_guidance: Remind that a rectangle has 4 sides total; two lengths and two breadths must be fenced.

MISC_PA_03.name: Shape-Perimeter Conservation Fallacy
MISC_PA_03.description: Believing shapes with identical perimeter must always have identical area.
MISC_PA_03.evidence_trigger: Believing a 5x3 rectangle (area 15) and a 4x4 square (area 16) have the same area because perimeter is 16.
MISC_PA_03.scaffolding_guidance: Show that squishing or stretching a boundary loop changes the interior capacity.

MISC_ALG_01.name: Sign Detachment from Coefficient
MISC_ALG_01.description: Dropping the negative sign in front of a variable term when identifying numerical coefficients.
MISC_ALG_01.scaffolding_guidance: The sign in front of a term belongs directly to its numerical coefficient factor.

MISC_ALG_02.name: Unlike Variable Concatenation / Conflation
MISC_ALG_02.description: Attempting to add coefficients of unlike terms together (e.g. 3x + 4y = 7xy).
MISC_ALG_02.evidence_trigger: Combining unlike variables into a single product term upon addition.
MISC_ALG_02.scaffolding_guidance: Like terms are items of the same fruit; 3 apples and 4 bananas cannot merge into 7 apple-bananas.

MISC_CIRC_01.name: Unipolar Current Fallacy (Single Wire)
MISC_CIRC_01.description: Believing electricity flows from only one terminal into a device without needing a complete return loop to the other terminal.
MISC_CIRC_01.evidence_trigger: Predicting a bulb will light with only one wire connecting the positive battery terminal to the bulb.
MISC_CIRC_01.scaffolding_guidance: Current requires an unbroken circular path (circuit) entering one terminal and returning through the other.

MISC_CIRC_02.name: Fused Bulb Power Blindness
MISC_CIRC_02.description: Thinking a bulb will light if wires and battery are connected properly even when its internal filament is broken.
MISC_CIRC_02.evidence_trigger: Assuming external switch closure guarantees lighting regardless of internal filament continuity.
MISC_CIRC_02.scaffolding_guidance: The tiny wire inside the bulb (filament) is part of the circuit path; if broken, the loop is open.

MISC_CIRC_03.name: Universal Conductor Fallacy (Material Ignorance)
MISC_CIRC_03.description: Believing any solid object placed in the circuit gap will conduct electric current.
MISC_CIRC_03.evidence_trigger: Predicting that plastic, rubber eraser, or dry wood will complete the circuit and turn on the bulb.
MISC_CIRC_03.scaffolding_guidance: Only conductors (metals like copper and iron) allow charges to pass; insulators block current flow.
